title: Elheen means *now*.
body: We are building the follow-up system for UAE service businesses. Every enquiry answered. Every quote followed up. Every payment collected.
caption:
الحين means "now" in the Gulf. It is also the whole idea.

Most service businesses here do great work and still lose jobs, not on price, but because a message waited too long or a quote was never chased.

Elheen keeps every enquiry, quote and payment in one place, and tells you each morning who to follow up, with the message already written.

Built in Dubai. Follow along as we build it.

title: Most jobs are not lost on price. *They are lost in a busy week.*
body: The enquiry that waited until tonight. The quote nobody chased. The visit nobody confirmed.
caption:
Think about the last three jobs you did not win.

How many were really about price? And how many went quiet because you were busy on site and the follow-up slipped?

The fix is not working harder. It is a simple system that reminds you who to reply to, who to confirm and who to chase, every single day.

Save this for the next busy week.

caption:

title: The 2 · 5 · 10 rule for quotes.
items: "Did you get a chance to look at it?"
Short and friendly. Offer a quick call.
Give them an easy way to say what is wrong.
"Shall I close it, or keep it open?"
A clear question gets a clear answer.
caption:
Sending the quote is not the end of the sale. It is the middle.

Most clients are not saying no. They are busy, comparing, or waiting for a nudge. Three short, polite messages are usually enough to get a real answer:

Day 2: did you get a chance to look at it?
Day 5: would you like to change anything?
Day 10: shall I close it, or keep it open?

Elheen reminds you on each day and writes the message for you.

Save this and try it on your open quotes this week.

title: A quote your client can *accept with one tap.*
caption:

They can also save it as a PDF or ask you a question on WhatsApp.

title: Ask 4 things *before a free site visit.*
items: Now, in 3 months, or just ideas?
You can price half the job from them.
body: Time-wasters show up before you drive across Dubai, not after.
caption:
A free site visit can cost you half a day.

Before you go, ask four simple questions: budget, start date, property type and a few photos. Serious clients answer them happily. People who are only collecting prices usually do not.

In Elheen these questions are built into your enquiry link, and each lead is marked as a good fit or one to check, based on your smallest job.

Save this for your team.

title: Extra work? Get it approved in writing. *Before it starts.*
body: "Can you also move the sink?" is how most payment arguments begin.
caption:
Halfway through a job, the client asks for something extra. You agree on site, do the work, and then the final payment turns into an argument.

The simple rule: price the extra work and get it approved in writing before you start. Every time, even for small things.

In Elheen you send it as a short quote on WhatsApp. The client approves it with their name, and it is added to the job and its payments automatically.
